name: capset
synopsis: int syscall(SYS_capset, cap_user_header_t hdrp, const cap_user_data_t datap);
description: capset is a Linux-specific system call used to set the capabilities of a thread. It operates on structures containing capability data and is subject to kernel API changes, making it non-portable; use portable interfaces like cap_set_proc(3) when possible.

parameters.name: hdrp
parameters.description: Pointer to a structure containing the capability version and the process or thread ID (pid)

parameters.name: datap
parameters.description: Pointer to a structure containing the effective, permitted, and inheritable capability sets

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: Bad memory address; hdrp must not be NULL, and datap may be NULL only when determining the preferred capability version.
One of the arguments was invalid, such as an unsupported version value.
Insufficient privileges, such as attempting to add a capability without proper permissions or modifying another thread's capabilities without CAP_SETPCAP.

bugs: A bug in kernels before Linux 2.6.11 could cause EPERM errors if a thread without CAP_SETPCAP tried to change its own capabilities by specifying a nonzero pid value.
versions: Linux, with significant changes in versions like 2.6.25 (introduced 64-bit capabilities) and 2.6.26 (introduced version 3).
